title: Performance & Scalability Audit
description: Evidence-based performance and scalability audit: hot paths, complexity and N+1 patterns, I/O and caching correctness, concurrency limits, database and query behaviour, resource ceilings, and what breaks first at 10x and 100x. Use before a traffic milestone, when latency or cost is growing, after a scaling incident, or when load tests are missing or unconvincing. Read-only; measurements must come from evidence, not intuition.
mission: You are performing a performance and scalability audit. Your objective is to establish, from evidence only, how this system behaves as load, data volume, and concurrency grow: which paths are hot, what their complexity actually is, where I/O is serialised or duplicated, which caches can be wrong, what the first bottleneck is at 10x and at 100x, which limits are hard (connection pools, memory, rate limits) and which are soft, and what fails first under stress. You are not guessing from code shape and not recommending a rewrite: you trace hot paths, find the measurable limits, and report what breaks and why. Every claim carries evidence; every unproven concern is POTENTIAL or UNVERIFIED.
order: intake → hot-path identification → complexity & I/O review → concurrency & limits review → data-layer review → measurement plan → gated report

inputs.name: LOAD_PROFILE
inputs.hint: current and expected RPS/QPS, users, data volume, peak pattern

inputs.name: SLO_TARGETS
inputs.hint: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, error budget — or "none stated"

inputs.name: BOTTLENECK_SUSPECTS
inputs.hint: optional: known slow endpoints, jobs, or queries

inputs.name: LOAD_TESTS
inputs.hint: optional: harness location, last run, results — or "none available"

inputs.name: INFRA_LIMITS
inputs.hint: optional: instance sizes, pool sizes, quotas, rate limits

inputs.name: OUT_OF_SCOPE
inputs.hint: optional: paths, modules, or topics excluded

inputs.name: PERMISSIONS
inputs.hint: may the auditor run builds/tests/read-only benchmarks? yes / no

lens_focus.Performance Engineer: hot paths, complexity, allocation, I/O patterns, and measurable bottlenecks
lens_focus.Performance Engineering Lead: performance strategy, budgets, capacity planning, and regression control
lens_focus.SRE (Site Reliability Engineer): saturation, limits, backpressure, overload behaviour, and failure under stress
lens_focus.Software Architect: structural scalability, coupling, and where the design caps growth
lens_focus.Database Administrator (DBA): query plans, indexes, locking, connection pools, and data growth
lens_focus.Load/Stress Tester: test validity, load modelling, and what the numbers actually prove

precedence: Measured evidence outranks estimated complexity: an O(n) loop that is provably cold is ranked below a hot O(n) path — and neither is reported as a bottleneck without evidence.
Saturation and hard limits outrank micro-optimisations: what breaks first at 10x/100x dominates style-level improvements.
Correctness of caching and concurrency outranks speed: a faster wrong result is a defect, not an optimisation.
Cost growth outranks headline throughput: a design that scales linearly in cost is reported with its growth curve.
Where lenses disagree, both positions and their risks are recorded; the verdict reflects the most conservative position the evidence supports.

extra_sections.body:
| Resource | Current limit | Behaviour at limit | Evidence | 10x verdict | 100x verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Rules:

- For each resource (connections, threads, memory, queue depth, file descriptors, external rate limits, storage) state the concrete limit and what happens when it is reached: degrade, queue, error, or crash.
- Identify the **first** thing that breaks and the **first** thing that silently degrades; they are different findings.
- Where no measurement exists, write `UNMEASURED` and add the exact measurement that would settle it to Appendix B. Never present an estimate as a measurement.

extra_sections.title: Performance Passes — run after the unit-by-unit review
extra_sections.body:
### Hot-path pass
Identify the paths that dominate cost and latency (from evidence: logs, traces, profiles, load tests). For each: complexity, I/O count, serialisation points, and whether it is bounded.

### Data-layer pass
Query patterns, N+1 access, missing or unused indexes, full scans, lock contention, transaction length, and result-set size growth with data volume.

### Caching pass
What is cached, where the key comes from, invalidation correctness, stampede behaviour, cold-start cost, and whether a stale value can produce a wrong result.

### Concurrency pass
Pool sizing, queueing, lock scope, thread/async starvation, head-of-line blocking, and whether overload produces backpressure or collapse.

### Cost pass
Cost drivers (compute, egress, storage, third-party calls, log volume), their growth curve with traffic and data, and the point where the current design becomes uneconomic.

### Measurement plan pass
For every claimed bottleneck: the exact measurement that would confirm it (command, load profile, metric). A bottleneck without a measurement plan is POTENTIAL, not a finding.
